newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Major, Kok to hold informal talks on Europe.
newsitem.headline: Major, Kok to hold informal talks on Europe.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major will visit The Hague on Tuesday for informal talks on Europe with his Dutch counterpart Wim Kok, the Dutch government said on Monday.
The Netherlands currently holds the presidency of the European Union.
A spokesman told Reuters that Kok had invited Major to dinner in The Hague for a private working visit. Major is expected to return to London later in the evening.
Kok, leader of the Dutch social-democratic Labour Party, angered Major last autumn when he signalled he would favour a Labour win in a British general election that has to be held by May.
The Dutch fear that Europe could loom large over a British election campaign, hampering progress on landmark EU treaty reforms due to be agreed at the Amsterdam summit in mid-June.
The spokesman also confirmed that Russian President Boris Yeltsin would visit The Hague on February 4 for talks with Kok.
He said a programme had yet to be finalised, but the two leaders were expected to discuss EU relations with Russia and may touch on the thorny issue of NATO enlargement.
Yeltsin's visit was set up by German Chancellor Helmut Kohl during his trip to Moscow at the weekend.
